rules.question: Which Form 1065 year applies to a fiscal year beginning July 1, 2025?
rules.whyItMatters: Sets the form, schedule and instruction revisions used by every other check.

fiscal years that begin in 2025 and end in 2026
rules.ruleOrLimit: The 2025 form covers fiscal years beginning in 2025 and ending in 2026. The fiscal year dates go in the header of Form 1065 and of each Schedule K-1.
rules.hangsApplication: The year begins July 1, 2025 and ends June 30, 2026, so the printed 2025 Form 1065, 2025 Schedule K-1 and 2025 instructions apply. Those dates go at the top of Form 1065 and both Schedules K-1.
rules.unresolved: Nothing on the form year. Whether June 30 is a permitted year is the separate check required-tax-year-june-30.

rules.question: When is the return due without an extension?

rules.hangsApplication: The tax year ended June 30, 2026. The 3rd month after is September, so the return was due September 15, 2026, a Tuesday by calendar math, so no weekend move applies. rules.ruleOrLimit: $255 per partner for each month or part of a month, up to 12 months, unless the failure is due to reasonable cause. The penalty also applies to a return that fails to show required information, and failure is measured against the due date including extensions.
rules.hangsApplication: With two partners the printed rate is $255 x 2 = $510 for each month or part of a month, up to $6,120 at 12 months. This is a rate, not an amount owed, because no filing date was supplied.

For returns due after December 31, 2026 (without regard to extensions) the base penalty rate is $260
rules.ruleOrLimit: The IRS sets the rate by the due date without regard to extensions: $255 for returns due in 2026 and $260 for returns due after 2026. Whether a return is late is still measured with regard to any extension. The Internal Revenue Manual is internal IRS guidance, not a regulation.

The months run from the extended date if Form 7004 was valid. $260 first reaches HANGS on the return for the year ended June 30, 2027.

changes: Form year: the 2025 Form 1065, 2025 Schedule K-1 and 2025 instructions replace the 2024 versions; Period Covered on page 5 names fiscal years that begin in 2025 and end in 2026.
Due date: September 15, 2026 (a Tuesday) replaces September 15, 2025; the six-month extended date is March 15, 2027, a Monday, so unlike last year's March 16, 2026 there is no weekend move.

Late filing penalty: the 2025 instructions print $255 per partner per month (2024 printed $245). Rev. Proc. 2024-40 sets $255 for returns required to be filed in 2026 and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 sets $260 for returns required to be filed in 2027, which first reaches HANGS on next year's return.

Section 448(c) gross receipts test: $31,000,000 for taxable years beginning in 2025 (Rev. Proc. 2024-40 section 2.31 and the 2025 instructions page 7), up from $30,000,000 for years beginning in 2024.
Form 7004: the Rev. December 2025 instructions now exist for a 2026 filing; the period is still generally 6 months and the IRS no longer sends approval notices.

Schedule K and K-1 line 19: the 2025 instructions re-coded distributions, with line 19a combining codes A, D and F and cash to non-service partners staying under code A; the 2025 Partner's Instructions What's New flags the same change.

New on the 2025 Form 1065: direct deposit lines 32b to 32d, an updated Schedule B question 19 on payments allocable to foreign partners, and new line 13 and line 20 codes from P.L. 119-21, none of which this partnership uses.

P.L. 119-21 (July 4, 2025): sec. 70430 widens the section 460(e) exception to residential construction contracts but applies only to contracts entered into in taxable years beginning after July 4, 2025, so a year beginning July 1, 2025 is not reached; sec. 70105 makes section 199A permanent for taxable years beginning after December 31, 2025, which does not alter this year's code Z reporting.

Reserves: this year has an increase in existing reserves plus payments against the opening balances, not a first-year balance, so the checks now cover the $4,900.00 paid against FY2025 provisions and the itemization of a net $3,700.00 on Schedule M-1 lines 4 and 7.
Organization costs: no reversal this year; the FY2025 $0.33 is carried inside opening tax capital of $12,299.67 and reappears in both tie-outs.
Schedule B-1 (Rev. August 2019), Form 1125-A (Rev. November 2024) and the Schedule M-3 instructions (Rev. November 2023) are unchanged and remain the current IRS files.

CFR citations now use the April 1, 2025 edition, whose running heads read 4-1-25 for every section cited; the 2024 U.S. Code edition is still the latest for the Code sections, so sec. 460 is quoted as it stood before P.L. 119-21, which is the text that applies to this year.
